newsitem.title: USA: IMF chief agrees that U.S. stock market looks high.
newsitem.headline: IMF chief agrees that U.S. stock market looks high.

text.p: IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus on Thursday seconded remarks made by his chief economist that the U.S. stock market looks to be high.

On Wednesday, International Monetary Fund chief economist Michael Mussa said that U.S. equity prices seem to be on the "rich side." Unlike remarks made by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan in December about "irrational exuberance" in asset markets, Mussa's comment had no impact on equity prices.

Camdessus told reporters that he was not surprised that prices had not reacted to what he called Mussa's "appropriate" remark and said this showed that the market had already responded appropriately to Greenspan's warnings.
U.S. stock prices have fallen from peak levels reached earlier this year, partly in response to the increase in interest rates last month by the U.S. central bank.
